items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: I did the Telephone Hour with Red Nichols

ctx.x: However -- at this time, I was in to the Hit Parade, which I did on weekends, and my reputation was growing there. I was fortunate to be able to read and cut a few parts, and I was hired by contractors, I had a reputation of working on the Hit Parade, which was a great show in those days -- I was hired, I ws what you'd call on the 'outside'. A freelance artist. But I was still working nights until four o'clock in the morning, which was killing at times.

And from the Hit Parade show, I would sub on the Perry Como Show and I did the Jack Benny Show -- these were all outside things -- the Jimmy Durante Show, these were all the beginning of television; television was just coming in strong then, and I was in on the ground floor. I did the Telephone Hour with Red Nichols, and I also did the Telephone Hour as a musician -- they hired me to keep time with several

of the modern features they did on those shows. I did the Steve Allen Tonight Show, and I did a great show that featured Louis Armstrong on CBS -- You Are There Show, and one of the titles was The Closing of Storyville, and that was a great feather in my bonnet. Louis Armstrong, Bobby Hackett -- I was with the Lawson-Haggard Band, and we emulated the original Dixieland -- the Original Dixieland Jazz Band was the name of it.
